headline: South Asia: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis in Islamabad meeting, Asif says
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis in Islamabad meeting, Asif says.
- Western Russia: Italian PM warns Ukraine after attack on Russian vessel in Mediterranean Sea.
- Africa: UN human rights chief warns of risk of escalating violence in western Nigeria.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
- Military Times, one day ago: Estimates of Russians killed in Ukraine surpass all combined US war deaths since WWI.
More than 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the war in Ukraine since Russia launched its full-scale war against the nation nearly five years ago.
- Military Times, one day ago: All USS George Washington CSG sailors returning from deployment to be provided ashore accommodations.
Sailors from the USS George Washington carrier strike group will be able to sleep in off-ship beds when they return from their roughly six-month deployment, the Navy said.
The Caribbean - bottom line: CMU trial could drag on until 2033, judge warns.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 21 hours ago: CMU trial could drag on until 2033, judge warns.
Senior Parish Court Judge Sanchia Burrell has warned that the trial of former Education Minister Ruel Reid and his co-accused could drag on until 2033 if the current pace of proceedings is maintained. Speaking yesterday in the Kingston and St Andrew Parish Court, Burrell pointed out that only about 10 to 11 of the 81 witnesses had so far given evidence, despite the matter having commenced in September 2025. “If the matter continues at this rate, we are not finishing this case until 2033,” Burrell warned.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

Italian PM Giorgia Meloni has warned against the war spreading to the Mediterranean following Ukrainian strikes on Russian vessels near Libya's port of Benghazi.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: Russian strike on Komyshuvakha: Slidstvo.Info uncovers details about perpetrators.
Slidstvo.Info uncovered details about Russian officers and pilots behind the 2 November airstrike on a school in Komyshuvakha that killed 72 people.
- The Moscow Times, 11 hours ago: Ukrainian Drone Strike Sparks Fire and Inflicts Serious Damage at Krasnodar Refinery.
The company operating the refinery said the attack took place during a maintenance stoppage that has been in place since a previous drone strike in September.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 10 hours ago: Russian drones attack Dnipropetrovsk Oblast 50 times.
Russian drones attacked two districts of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast more than 50 times on 26 November, damaging businesses, a kindergarten and infrastructure.

- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: Trump diverges from NATO statement, emphasizing Ukraine mustn’t expand war.
The U.S. president's unilateral tweak of a joint missive occurred days after Kyiv struck a Russian warship off the coast of Libya.
- Balkan Insight, 10 hours ago: European Parliament Backs Vukovar Anniversary Resolution Criticising Serbia.
Despite criticism by Serbia's student movement, MEPs voted to adopt a resolution marking the 35th anniversary of the Croatian town's fall in 1991 and urging Belgrade to open its war archives to help find the remaining missing persons.
- Balkan Insight, 17 hours ago: Croatia’s War Victims, Mass Graves Documented by New Independent Research.
At an event in Zagreb, BIRN launched the Croatia-based research for its Bitter Land database of wartime mass graves, while NGO Documenta presented its new Croatian Book of Remembrance.
- Balkan Insight, 20 hours ago: Albania’s Rebuild After 2019 Earthquake Still a Work in Progress.
Seven years after an earthquake killed 51 people and razed 11,000 homes in Albania, hundreds of people are still waiting for a new home.

[Nyasa Times] Malawi's film industry is set for a glamorous three-day showcase after Films Association of Malawi (Fama) president Dorothy Kingston declared that everything is in place for the Malawi Film Gala and Awards, which runs from Thursday to Saturday at BICC in Lilongwe.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis in Islamabad meeting, Asif says.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 12 hours ago: Makkah pact nations to discuss conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis in Islamabad meeting, Asif says.
The Makkah pact nations will discuss the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Houthi fighters in Yemen when officials from the mutual defence agreement meet in Islamabad on Thursday, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif told AFP. Asif said the “continuous turmoil south of Saudi Arabia will obviously be one agenda point in the meeting and it is very important”, confirming that defence and foreign ministers from the Gulf kingdom, Turkiye and Pakistan would attend.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 19 hours ago: Security forces kill 12 India-sponsored terrorists in multiple IBOs in Balochistan: ISPR.
Security forces killed 12 India-sponsored terrorists in four separate intelligence-based operations (IBOs) in Balochistan between November 20 and 23, the military’s media wing said on Thursday. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), security forces targeted a terrorist hideout in Nushki district on November 20. Following an intense exchange of fire, eight terrorists belonging to the Indian-backed Fitna-al-Hindustan were killed. Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the site, the ISPR added.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 13 hours ago: Meta battles political storm in India as Congress party sues, stages protests.
India’s main opposition party, the Indian National Congress, has sued Meta and the federal government, saying that an automated content-removal system is blocking political posts and images of ​opposition leader Rahul Gandhi ahead of state elections. The filing takes a week-long Congress campaign against Meta from the streets to the courtroom, and highlights Prime Minister ‌Narendra Modi’s automated takedown mandate, under which the Facebook and Instagram parent has restricted more than 5.4 million posts in the first half of 2026, up from about 70,000 in all of 2025.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: AJK govt removes Rawalakot mayor over allegations of 'anti-state activities'.
MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government on Thursday removed Rawalakot Mayor Abdul Naeem Khan from office and terminated his membership of the municipal corporation over his alleged “involvement in anti-state activities”. A notification issued by the Local Government and Rural Development Department said the action was taken under Section 23(2) of the Local Government Act, 1990. According to a separate notification by the AJK Home Department, dated Nov 15, Khan’s name was among those placed on the Fourth Schedule under Section 16 of the AJK Anti-Terrorism Act.
Asia - bottom line: Iran denies role in drone attack that killed Italians in Kuwait.
- South China Morning Post - China, NDTV - Top Stories, The Hindu - International, just now: Iran denies role in drone attack that killed Italians in Kuwait.
A drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians working on an air defence system on Thursday, marking the first fatal strike in the Gulf state for months. Both Italy and Kuwait confirmed the deaths, blaming the attack on Iran. But Tehran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi insisted in calls to his Kuwaiti and Italian counterparts that it was not behind the deadly strike. Iran has in the last week ratcheted up attacks on Kuwait and Gulf neighbour Bahrain while it continues to fight the...
- South China Morning Post - China, 17 hours ago: PLA overhauls joint training after drills expose coordination gaps.
China’s military is overhauling how its various services train together as joint exercises continue to expose shortcomings in the People’s Liberation Army’s ability to fight as an integrated force. In the latest example, a navy destroyer flotilla under the PLA’s Eastern Theatre Command changed how it trains with other services following drills in which airforce jets were twice judged to have been “shot down” by friendly forces. A PLA Rocket Force unit also struggled to guide strikes against...
- South China Morning Post - China, 14 hours ago: Russian court jails Colombian fighter for 20 years over Ukraine war role.
A court in Ukraine’s Moscow-annexed Donetsk region jailed a Colombian for 20 years, saying he was a mercenary fighting for Kyiv, Russia said on Thursday. The Russian Prosecutor General’s Office said the court “has handed down a verdict in the criminal case against 33-year-old Colombian national Cristian Morales Mendoza”, adding he was “a mercenary in an armed conflict”. Both Moscow and Kyiv have recruited thousands of foreigners in their armies since Russia launched its offensive in Ukraine...
- South China Morning Post - China, 16 hours ago: Tai Po fire: remembering the victims.
Hong Kong is still healing, one year after a devastating inferno engulfed Tai Po’s Wang Fuk Court residential complex. Survivors are trying to move forward while grieving loved ones – parents, spouses, siblings and children – whom they lost without the chance to say goodbye. The South China Morning Post has created a full-page infographic to remember the 168 people killed in the fire. The petals symbolise the lives lost – people held forever in the hearts of their families, friends and the...
India - bottom line: 'Nuclear holocaust' risk: Trump claims Iran missiles can reach Europe.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: 'Nuclear holocaust' risk: Trump claims Iran missiles can reach Europe.
US President Donald Trump expressed concerns about Iran's missile capabilities and the prospect of regional instability. He stated that Iran could potentially launch nuclear attacks on Israel and surrounding countries in the Middle East. Trump emphasized the necessity of achieving peace in the region while supporting local countries until they can defend themselves. He noted that Iran does not currently possess a nuclear weapon, which is significant under international agreements.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Zelensky Warns Of New Russian Mass Strike In "Coming Days".
Russian forces have been subjecting Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities to virtually continuous, round-the-clock attacks since September.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: US techie likely behind dozens of Mumbai bomb threat held in Tamil Nadu.
Sharath Subramanian Shankar, a 28-year-old techie from Tamil Nadu, is implicated in sending over 1,500 hoax emails. These emails warned of attacks on significant locations in Mumbai, including the BMC office and the Bombay Stock Exchange. He was detained by Tamil Nadu police after returning from the US based on intelligence from Mumbai police. Another suspect, Ankit Shankhwar, is being investigated for supplying fake email accounts used in these threats.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: India playing leading role in global war on terror, says Amit Shah.
Amit Shah, the Union home minister, reaffirmed India's unwavering dedication to fighting terrorism while honoring the memories of those affected by the 26/11 attacks. He praised the bravery of both soldiers and innocent civilians, asserting that the Modi government’s unwavering stance against terrorism is garnering global recognition. Shah also highlighted that united action is essential, as terrorism remains a grave threat to humanity.

Australia - bottom line: Outback city's first new hotel in decades being manufactured 4,600km away.
- ABC News Australia, 4 hours ago: Outback city's first new hotel in decades being manufactured 4,600km away.
Construction of a new four-star, $40 million hotel for Australia's biggest outback city is progressing at a factory in Malaysia, as modular building techniques increase in popularity to meet ongoing shortages of skilled tradespeople in regional areas.
